records.omission_quote: The direct Narrow-Control test that we employed has been used in studies by Wilcox and her collaborators as well. The Results test and report the corresponding high- versus low-power poser overconfidence comparison. Fast et al. is a distinct empirical original and is not represented by supplied shipped row 1047, which is Carney et al. (2010).

records.omission_quote: High-power (M = 0.14, SD = 0.53) posers did not have higher post-manipulation levels of overconﬁdence than low-power posers (M = −0.01, SD = 0.51), F(1,104) = 0.26, p = 0.61, d = 0.099, r = 0.05.
records.identity_quote: Building from these ﬁndings, Fast and colleagues (2012) reported ﬁve experiments that used multiple instantiations of power – including manipulations via episodic recall tasks, role assignment, and extant work related power – where they found high power to be associated with overconﬁdent decision-making.
